summary: Incumbent Democratic Gov. Josh Green ran for reelection and won a second term, defeating Republican Gary Cordery.

candidates.name: Josh Green
candidates.bio: Josh Green is a Democrat and a physician who has served as governor of Hawaii since 2022. He worked as an emergency room doctor, served as a state legislator, and was lieutenant governor from 2018 to 2022.

positions.summary: Says he delivered the biggest middle-class tax cut in Hawaii history, including a doubled earned income tax credit and food tax credit.
Says he is lowering healthcare costs, will cover Obamacare subsidies for families who depend on them, and is bringing nearly $1 billion in federal money to rural health.
Points to the Green Fee, an 11% tax on tourist accommodations, as the state's largest dedicated funding source for climate action.
Signed bills in July 2026 creating annual salary step increases for teachers and covering 95 percent of community college students' unmet direct costs through Hawaii Promise.
Signed Senate Bill 1 in 2023, which writes abortion protections into state law and protects providers and patients who travel to Hawaii from states with stricter laws.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called) Original summary noted the Republican ticket (with running mate Daniel Anthony) had 26.1% in the latest tally. Vote shares are from the Wikipedia article 2026 Hawaii gubernatorial election (384,703 votes in total); the page did not state what share of the vote was counted.
